title_en: Bloomberg’s Jim on Europe’s Active ETF Outlook
title_zh: 彭博 Henry Jim 谈欧洲主动型 ETF 的前景
description: Europe’s active ETF market is expanding rapidly, but rising product launches don’t necessarily signal broad investor adoption. In this episode of Inside Active, host David Cohne, mutual fund and active management analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, speaks with Henry Jim, ETF analyst at BI, about what’s driving the market’s growth and why its development is likely to differ from the US. They discuss how issuer-led launches and solutions-based strategies are shaping the category, why Europe’s fragmented distribution system and investment culture remain important hurdles, and how private banks and white-label providers could broaden adoption. They also explore why fixed income may be a natural fit for active ETFs, what JPMorgan has done to gain traction in Europe, how ETFs could eventually pressure traditional active-management fees and what would need to happen for active ETFs to capture a meaningfully larger share of the European market. Recorded Aug. 19.

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond sound bites and headlines and looks deeper into their processes, challenges and philosophies and security selection. I'm David cone I, Lead Mutual Fund and Active Research at Bloomberg Intelligence. Active ETFs are becoming one of the fastest growing parts of the European fund market. The category is still relatively small compared with the broader ETF industry, but growth is accelerated as more asset managers launch active strategies and the ETF wrapper, and more investors begin to use them across equities, fixed income, and other parts of the market. What makes Europe especially interesting is that its market structure is very different from the United States. Distribution is more fragmented, investor behavior very significantly by country, and traditional active mutual funds remain deeply in So the question is not simply whether active ETFs can grow, but how large the opportunity can become, which strategies are best suited to the wrapper, and what will ultimately drive adoption. So today I wanted to explore where the European active ETF market stands, what's behind its recent growth, which managers and strategies are gaining traction and what could shape the next phase of development. Joining me to discuss that is my colleague Henry Jim ETF, analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence where he covers the European ETF industry. Henry, thanks for joining me, Hi, David, thanks having me. So let's start with the big picture. How would you characterize the active ETF market in Europe today? And you know, where are we in its development compared with the US.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听《Inside Active》。这是一档聚焦主动管理人（active manager）的播客，不止于只言片语和新闻标题，而是深入探讨他们的投资流程（investment process）、挑战、投资理念（investment philosophy）和证券选择（security selection）。我是 David Cohne，在 Bloomberg Intelligence 负责共同基金（mutual fund）与主动管理研究。主动型交易所交易基金（active ETF）正成为欧洲基金市场增长最快的领域之一。与更广泛的交易所交易基金（exchange-traded fund, ETF）行业相比，这一类别的规模仍然相对较小，但随着越来越多资产管理公司（asset manager）通过 ETF 载体（ETF wrapper）推出主动策略，以及越来越多投资者开始将其用于股票、固定收益（fixed income）及其他市场领域，其增长正在加速。欧洲市场尤其有意思，是因为其市场结构与美国大不相同。渠道分销（distribution）更加碎片化，投资者行为因国家而有显著差异，传统主动管理共同基金依然根基深厚。因此，问题不只是主动型 ETF 能否增长，还包括这一机会最终能有多大、哪些策略最适合 ETF 载体，以及最终将由什么推动市场采用（adoption）。所以，今天我想探讨欧洲主动型 ETF 市场目前处于什么阶段，近期增长背后的原因，哪些管理人和策略正在获得市场认可，以及什么因素可能塑造其下一发展阶段。今天与我讨论这些问题的是我的同事 Henry Jim。他是 Bloomberg Intelligence 的 ETF 分析师，负责覆盖欧洲 ETF 行业。Henry，感谢你参加节目。嗨，David，谢谢你邀请我。我们先从大局谈起。你会如何描述如今欧洲的主动型 ETF 市场？与美国相比，我们目前处于怎样的发展阶段？

turns.en: How would I characterize it? It's still alive in kicking, if I can say, but a lot of those less kicking than one would assume based on the numbers that we saw in the past couple of years. And what I mean by that is, indeed, assets are growing, number of issuers are growing, number of etf they're all growing. But we really have to take a look at the type of funds that are being launched, who's launching them, and the growth rate. So I would say it's still growing, It's still going to grow, but we're gonna see some volatility and there's a growth rate in the coming months. And I guess we'll dive more into this over the podcast.
turns.zh: 我会怎样描述它？可以说，它依然充满活力，只是活跃程度远没有人们根据过去几年看到的数字所想象的那么高。我的意思是，资产规模确实在增长，发行人（issuer）数量在增加，ETF 数量也在增加，一切都在增长。但我们确实必须看看推出的是什么类型的基金、由谁推出，以及增长率如何。所以我会说，它仍在增长，未来还会继续增长，但未来几个月的增长率会出现波动率（volatility）上升的情况。我想，我们会在这期播客中进一步讨论这个问题。

turns.en: Okay, so you know obviously there's still you know, a relatively small part of the European you know, ETF assets in general. But you know, as you said, they are growing. You know, what is driving the acceleration.
turns.zh: 好的。显然，与整个欧洲 ETF 资产相比，它们所占的比重仍然相对较小。但正如你所说，它们正在增长。是什么推动了这种加速？

turns.en: Well, actually let's go through some of the numbers first. In terms of driving the numbers, well, there's a lastly check. It was about four hundred distinct active ETFs out of about twenty seven hundred in Europe. The four hundred are active. I think they managed assets were about one hundred and twenty five million euros, so that's about one hundred, one hundred and thirty five million dollars in assets across all four hundred, so on a per ETF basis a pretty small and in terms of growth rate, in twenty twenty four we had sixty new active ETFs launched and that jumped to one hundred and sixty new ones one hundred and fifty to one hundred and sixty and twenty twenty five. But this year we're probably not going to breach one hundred and fifty, so I would say the growth rate it's kind of a plateoy right now. Right. I think the drivers for the initial jump in launches and in assets were we're actually an issuer from the issuer side. But what I mean by that is they a lot of issuers really came to the market seeing opportunities, see what was going on in the States, and they launched a lot and they had a really good distribution push, and that gave an initial boost to active ETFs. Another thing that would have to be careful of is what is an active etf. Currently we're working on a taxonomy where we're here in Europe working a better taxonomy for active ETFs. Meaning a lot of the successful active ets, the ones that are tagged activitfs are actually I would say almost non passive.
turns.zh: 其实，我们先看一些数字。谈到这些数字背后的驱动因素，据我最近一次核查，欧洲约 2,700 只不同的 ETF 中，大约有 400 只是主动型 ETF。这 400 只主动型 ETF 的管理资产规模（assets under management, AUM）约为 125 million 欧元，也就是全部 400 只合计约 135 million 美元。因此，平均到每只 ETF 上，规模相当小。就增长率而言，2024 年新推出了 60 只主动型 ETF；到 2025 年，这一数字跃升至 160 只左右，大约为 150 至 160 只。但今年，我们可能不会突破 150 只。因此我会说，增长率目前有些进入平台期。最初推动产品发行数量和资产规模跃升的因素，我认为其实来自发行人一侧。我的意思是，许多发行人看到其中的机会，也看到美国正在发生什么，于是大量推出产品，并大力推动渠道分销，这给主动型 ETF 带来了最初的提振。我们还必须谨慎看待另一个问题：究竟什么算主动型 ETF？目前，我们正在研究一套分类体系，也就是在欧洲为主动型 ETF 建立一套更完善的分类方法。原因在于，许多成功的主动型 ETF，也就是被标记为主动型 ETF 的产品，实际上在我看来更接近“非被动”产品。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: They do have exposure to broad equity regional in the CES, they try to keep close in the performance, but they either have an option's overlay or it's an index plus strategy. Right, so pure stock picking or bond picking ets aren't that much in vogue yet.
turns.zh: 它们确实提供对广泛区域股票指数的敞口，力求保持与指数表现接近，但要么叠加了期权叠加策略（options overlay），要么采用指数增强策略。也就是说，纯粹依靠选股（stock picking）或债券选择（bond picking）的 ETF 目前还没有那么流行。

turns.en: Okay, So you know, I kind of separate them, you know in the States, you know, between traditional you know, security selection both on the bond and equity side, and then what I call new active you know, the options overlay outcome type stuff. turns.en: In terms of adoption, there's two ways looking at In terms of adoption from the investor base, I don't think it's really that big of an adoption yet. Like I said before, it's mostly issuer push right now, and it is of course concentrating a few of these options over la ets, right Yeah, it's it's it's mostly from issuers sort of trying to launch it get ahead in the active ets space. turns.en: And so do you think you know, as these grow, they're going to kind of take assets to you know, obviously active mutual funds are pretty big in Europe just like they were in the US, you know, decades ago. Do you think it's going to come from active mutual funds or is it you know, you think they'd be kind of a new market. It's created a bit of both.

turns.en: I think the the push by money managers general will continue and that will bring a lot more money into active ETFs. So they're either launching ets share classes of their existing mutual fund strategies, or they're launching atfs mimicking their strategies. That set us right up. We've seen those. We didn't see brand new active ets being launched, So that's one. But I think it's not going to be like in the States. What we're missing here in Europe is an investment culture still. Like in the US, think it was a perfect sore for ETFs. We had the four to one k's being launched in the eighties and then people took their investments more, you know, in their own power. We had a decreasing interest rates, and also we had declining confidence and social security being able to maintain us in retirement. What we see here in Europe is still we have a very large middle class that is still fairly comfortable. They are just you know, riding their wave of wealth accumulation stage. It's the young people who are starting to realize that or starting to question whether their pension will sustain them in retirement, and those are the ones who are starting to look at other ways of saving away for the retirement. Obviously, the governments here the EU is also looking at ways of motivating people to invest more of their own as well to take some pressure away from their pressure payments.
turns.zh: 我认为，资产管理人（money manager）整体上的推动会持续下去，并将为主动型 ETF 带来更多资金。他们要么为现有共同基金策略推出 ETF 份额类别（share class），要么推出模仿其现有策略的 ETF。这就自然衔接上了。我们已经见过这些做法，也看到了全新的主动型 ETF 推出。这是一个方面。但我认为欧洲不会像美国那样发展。欧洲仍然缺少的是投资文化。美国的情况可以说是 ETF 发展的完美风暴：20 世纪 80 年代推出了 401(k) 计划，此后人们越来越多地把投资掌握在自己手中；利率不断下降；同时，人们对于社会保障制度能否在退休后继续维持其生活的信心也在减弱。我们在欧洲看到的是，这里仍有规模非常庞大的中产阶层，生活依然相当安稳。他们只是继续沿着财富积累阶段的轨迹前行。开始意识到、或者开始质疑养老金能否支撑自己退休生活的是年轻人，他们正着手寻找其他方式为退休储蓄。显然，这里的各国政府和欧盟也在设法鼓励人们增加自主投资，从而减轻养老金支付压力。

turns.en: But that.

These are like late twenties, early thurds folks who are just starting to accumulate their wealth, so they don't really have that much of an impact yet on ATF asset and flows, right, and so if we don't have like in the States, it was first it was passive ETFs and now we're looking at the UH investors starting to go into activity tests for different reasons. There's the new ones, the solutions, why, I says sir, But we haven't even reached that stage yet in Europe. I don't think there's going to be a major boost in active ETF assets in the next five years. Let's say.
turns.zh: 新兴的零售投资者群体仍然很小。这些人大约二十七八岁到三十岁出头，才刚刚开始积累财富，因此目前对 ETF 资产规模和基金资金流（fund flow）的影响其实并不大。美国最初是被动投资（passive investing）ETF 发展起来，现在又看到美国投资者出于不同原因开始进入主动型 ETF，包括新产品、解决方案等。但欧洲甚至还没有走到那个阶段。我认为，至少在未来 5 年，主动型 ETF 的资产规模不会出现大幅跃升。

turns.en: Okay, now that's fair enough, and yeah, I'm kind of glad you brought that up, because I think people often think that what happened in the US is going to be is repeatable in other regions, and so you know, obviously it doesn't sound like it's going to follow the same path. So it's definitely something to watch.
turns.zh: 好的，这很合理。我也很高兴你提到这一点，因为人们常常认为美国发生的事情可以在其他地区复制。显然，欧洲听起来不会走同一条路，所以这绝对值得关注。

turns.en: I think all the ingredients are there, but what's really going to like that spark is the investment culture. Right. Yeah.

turns.en: So you know, if you talk about that, you know or not inside of the culture in Europe, but just you know Europe's kind of fragmented distribution model, you know, with inducements and retro sessions and you know, different markets. Is that kind of explained why active bgfs haven't grown as fast.
turns.zh: 那么，如果谈到这一点，不只是欧洲的投资文化，还包括欧洲碎片化的渠道分销模式，以及其中的销售激励费、返佣和不同市场。这是否解释了主动型 ETF 没有更快增长的原因？

turns.en: That's only part of the the reason because these inducements, the fragmentation of the markets, those are those are it's put in place by by local money managers who have like a full possession of the of the value chain right from product to distribution to management, et cetera. And they have the relationious with their clients. And these clients who appreciate this full touch, if you will, are people who are have a community the wealth. You know, people in my age range or or are older. Right, so whether or not they have induceds I think they're they're quite bound to their advisor or to their bank already, right, So I think that only part of the accounts for why ETFs are not taking off. I don't think they're the main barrier, to be honest. If anything, I think the the lack of demand for investments by the individual investor is what's keeping the inducements at and inducements and retrocessus in place.
turns.zh: 这只是部分原因。因为这些销售激励费和市场碎片化，是由当地资产管理人维持的；这些机构从产品、渠道分销到管理等环节，掌控着完整的价值链，而且与客户保持着关系。重视这种全方位服务的客户，都是已经积累了一定财富的人，也就是和我年龄相仿或更年长的人。因此，无论是否存在销售激励费，我认为他们都已经与自己的顾问或银行形成了相当牢固的关系。所以，我认为这只能部分解释 ETF 为何没有起飞。坦率地说，我不认为这是主要障碍。要说有什么的话，我认为，个人投资者缺乏投资需求，才是销售激励费和返佣得以继续存在的原因。

turns.en: So if we kind of go further, what about other types of investors, you know, could they help really unlock growth for active ETFs, whether that's like wealth platforms, banks, institutional investors.
turns.zh: 如果进一步讨论，其他类型的投资者又如何？财富管理平台、银行或机构投资者能否帮助真正释放主动型 ETF 的增长潜力？

turns.en: Sure, we don't have many too many platforms that we do in states, but I would definitely like private banks, robo advisors. I think those are really good entry into ets and really boost the market. So for private bank for example, as I mentioned, there is a growing there's still a strong middle class, and there are these young folks who are who are building their wealth and they're looking at investment options, and I don't think they want to use their parents' model of having an advisor and who charge a lot of fees, right, So I think private banks and they're starting there's a there's a few startups here already from private banks who are targeting these people, the younger affluid mass affluid I think they call them right and giving the bare basis of a bank self wet wealth management advice mostly online and put portfolios right. So private banks I think is one channel. Uh grobal advisors of course those are those are mainly those who will be mainly passive. And another one I see are the white label VTF providers actually, because we have a lot of money managers in Europe who are looking to get into the ETF industry, but they see the costs involved and the fragmented distribution and trying to look for the clients, but they still want to get in because one they want to say they have an ETF, but more importantly to start a track record for their active strategies. Right, So they're going through the white labels to establish a record, and we're seeing a lot of launches from the white label providers for existing money managers in their active strategies. So when you ask them, are the incumbents or or the newcomers who are really getting into activities, I think it's coming from both sides. The incumbents the top, the top three. You know, I Shares, Deutsche Banks, X Trackers, a MUNDI. They're launching their activities Fidelity for example. But then you have HONEYTF launching a bunch of active ETFs for I would say smaller asset managers active managers, but incumbents and mutual funds.
turns.zh: 当然。欧洲不像美国那样有很多平台，但我肯定认为私人银行和智能投顾会成为进入 ETF 的良好渠道，并真正推动市场发展。以私人银行为例，正如我所说，这里仍有实力雄厚的中产阶层，也有一批正在积累财富、寻找投资选择的年轻人。我不认为他们想沿用父母那种模式，即聘请收费很高的顾问。因此，我认为私人银行是一个渠道。现在这里已经出现了几家私人银行领域的初创公司，瞄准这些较年轻的富裕和大众富裕客户——我想他们是这样称呼的——为其提供银行的基础服务、主要在线完成的自主财富管理建议以及投资组合。智能投顾当然是另一个渠道，不过它们主要仍会采用被动投资。另一个机会其实是白标服务商（white-label provider），因为欧洲有很多资产管理人希望进入 ETF 行业，但他们看到了相关成本、碎片化的渠道分销环境，以及寻找客户的难度。尽管如此，他们仍然希望进入这一行业，一是因为他们想表明自己拥有 ETF，更重要的是，他们希望为自己的主动策略建立业绩记录。因此，他们正通过白标服务商来建立业绩记录。我们看到，白标服务商正在为现有资产管理人及其主动策略推出很多产品。所以，如果你问真正进入主动型 ETF 的是现有龙头还是新进入者，我认为两边都有。现有龙头包括前三大机构，比如 iShares、Deutsche Bank 旗下的 Xtrackers 和 Amundi，它们都在推出自己的主动型 ETF；Fidelity 也是如此。与此同时，HANetf 正在为一批规模较小的资产管理公司和主动管理人推出许多主动型 ETF，而这些机构本身又是共同基金领域的现有参与者。

But then again these aren't exactly actively managed, they're just non passive, right, These are defined outcome ETFs in terms of a truly true active I really think fixed income will be the natural space for for actively managed ETFs because the fixed income market in Europe, if not globally, is also very fermative. I think it's just much more opportunities in fixed income.
turns.zh: 就目前而言，作为解决方案的主动型 ETF 最有意义，也就是我们刚才谈到的那些“非被动”产品。我之所以这么说，是因为欧洲虽然没有真正意义上的投资文化，却有使用结构性票据（structured note）的传统。顾问会为客户设计专属产品，使之与客户的负债等相匹配。我认为，很多缓冲型 ETF（buffer ETF）、提供期权费收入（premium income）的产品以及确定结果型 ETF（defined-outcome ETF），都会非常契合这个市场。但话说回来，它们并不完全属于主动管理，只能算是非被动产品，也就是确定结果型 ETF。至于真正的主动管理，我确实认为固定收益会自然成为主动型 ETF 的用武之地，因为欧洲乃至全球的固定收益市场同样非常碎片化。我认为，固定收益领域的机会要多得多。

turns.en: Yeah. No, I'm glad you read that fixed income because I mean, obviously activists in general is pretty well suited. You know, indexes or bondingexes typically have some unusual characteristics, and you know, I think active managers, you know, are able to do things, you know, look at duration and you know credit selection that seems to they're able to provide alpha, you know, if we take aside, you know, bond indexes being easier to beat. But you know, so you know, it's interesting you think active fixed income could really be a big part of the European market. What about like alternatives? Is that something? Because I think we're starting to see that a little bit in the stage. You think eventually, you know, retail investors getting access to kind of alternatives and the ETF wrapper eventually.
turns.zh: 是的。我很高兴你提到固定收益，因为主动型固定收益管理总体上显然非常适合这种形式。指数，或者说债券指数，通常具有一些不寻常的特征；我认为主动管理人能够采取一些措施，比如考察久期（duration）并进行信用选择（credit selection），从而似乎可以创造超额收益（alpha）——即便我们暂且不谈债券指数本身更容易被战胜这一点。所以，你认为主动型固定收益确实可能成为欧洲市场的重要组成部分，这很有意思。那么另类投资呢？这是一个机会吗？因为我认为，我们在美国已经开始看到一些这样的产品。你认为，零售投资者最终会通过 ETF 载体获得另类投资敞口吗？

turns.en: Eventually, but that would be like maybe ten years on the road. Again, it goes back to it goes back to like if you if you have someone in the States to who is investing in the market, you can talk about alternatives and fix income and commodity, et cetera. But you take a regular person off the shoot here you ask about, you know, asset classes. I don't think you get a very you don't. You'll get more black stares at that an answer, to be honest, right, So it's not that they're not interested, it's just that it's not even on the radar right now. First step is investments, and then we'll talking about rappers and deal with aught about strategies and we're just barely breaking through the next step too right now.
turns.zh: 最终会，但那可能要等到 10 年以后。这仍然要回到同一个问题：如果面对一位在美国进行市场投资的人，你可以跟他谈另类投资、固定收益、大宗商品等。但如果你在欧洲街头随便找一个普通人，问他有关资产类别的问题，坦率地说，我认为你得到的茫然注视会多于真正的回答。这并不是说他们不感兴趣，而是这个问题目前根本还没有进入他们的视野。第一步是开始投资，之后我们才会谈载体，再之后才会谈策略，而现在我们才刚刚勉强迈入第二步。

turns.en: Okay, And so you know you had mentioned a couple of the different you know firms launching, but you know, kind of when I just took a look at the you know, our dashboard on b I E t F and B I E t F, I S see, it looked like JP Morgan's built kind of a big position in European active ETFs in terms of assets. What do you think it got right early on that other traditional managers didn't. Is it just kind of they jumped jumped ahead and kind of dove in first.
turns.zh: 好的。你刚才提到了几家推出产品的公司。我查看了 BI ETF 和 BI ETF IS 上的仪表板，按资产规模来看，JPMorgan 似乎已经在欧洲主动型 ETF 市场建立了很大的优势。它早期做对了什么，而其他传统管理人没有做到？只是因为它抢先一步、率先全力进入这个市场吗？

turns.en: Yeah, No, Jpmrior has done really well here in Europe. I think what they did right, they had a good combination of product so solutions based. I think Jpmorriy did real well because they they had a very they could articulate very well the problem that they were tiring to solve and the solution that they were offering. Right. So when I mentioned you know, you have outcome ETFs or solutions based. Although the JB. Morgan products they also have some uh some buffer in them, some some premium income. They are more solutions based, so there is some active up stock picking as well. Right, it's a very complex product, but they were able to articulate all the different problems they were trying to solve with it right. And I think that is something that other issuers have not been as a three to two let me think of the word not as a and that's something that other issuers have not been as adept in doing and being able to able to frame the problem and also to offer the solution with the ETF instead. I think I find some other issuers they go into the product structure, they go into ETFs, and I think there's just a lot of information there, whereas JP Morgan is pretty focused on what they're selling to what clients.
turns.zh: 是的。JPMorgan 在欧洲确实做得非常好。我认为它做对的一点，是拥有很好的解决方案型产品组合。JPMorgan 做得很好的原因在于，它能够非常清楚地阐明自己试图解决的问题，以及所提供的解决方案。我刚才提到过结果导向型 ETF 或解决方案型产品。JPMorgan 的产品虽然也包含一些缓冲机制和期权费收入，但它们更偏向解决方案型，因此也会进行一些主动选股。这是一种非常复杂的产品，但 JPMorgan 能够把它试图解决的各种问题都讲清楚。我认为，其他发行人在这方面不像它那么——让我想想这个词——不像它那么娴熟：既能界定问题，也能用 ETF 提供解决方案。我发现，其他一些发行人会深入谈产品结构、深入谈 ETF，信息量非常大；相比之下，JPMorgan 非常专注于自己向哪些客户销售什么产品。

turns.en: Right, Okay, and so you know, obviously the market is still pretty small. But for managers coming in today, whether that's on their own or through white labels, how difficult do you think it's going to be for them to catch kind of the bigger firms Now.
turns.zh: 对。好的。显然，这个市场仍然很小。但对于今天才进入市场的管理人，无论是自行进入还是通过白标服务商进入，你认为它们要追赶较大的公司会有多困难？

turns.en: It really depends what you mean by catching up. If you mean catching up in terms of assets, I think that's going to take a tremendous effort and no guarante they're going to succeed anyway. I think national champions such as Intesla Sanpaolo in Italy might have a chance since they they own the ow value chain, but smaller money managers to reach the level of the top three the top five will be very difficult. What I do see for traditional mutual fund active managers coming in is to really carve out their niche. If they have a good combination of of.
turns.zh: 这实际上取决于你所说的“追赶”是什么意思。如果是指在资产规模上追赶，我认为这需要付出巨大的努力，而且无论如何也不能保证成功。意大利 Intesa Sanpaolo 这样的全国性龙头或许有机会，因为它们掌控着整条价值链；但对规模较小的资产管理人来说，要达到前三大或前五大机构的水平会非常困难。我认为，传统主动管理共同基金管理人进入这一市场时，真正可行的方向是开辟自己的细分领域。如果他们能够很好地结合……

turns.en: Uh of of of a good product set with a very well structured distribution effort, I think they may have a big chance of transferring their current assets into ETFs right and build them that for for for a bigger ATF business.
turns.zh: ……把优质的产品组合与结构非常完善的渠道分销工作结合起来，我认为他们就很有机会把现有资产转入 ETF，并以此为基础建立更大的 ETF 业务。

turns.en: Right, So let me ask you this, then, you know, do you think every large asset manager in Europe eventually needs an ETF lineup or do you think they'll be They'll still be firms that will be still successful, you know, doing only mutual funds, you know, like down the line.
turns.zh: 对。那么我这样问吧：你认为欧洲每一家大型资产管理公司最终都需要拥有一套 ETF 产品线吗？还是说，从长远来看，仍会有一些只做共同基金也能持续成功的公司？

turns.en: Personally, maybe in bias, I think every large ass manager should have ets period. And the reason I say that is because you can stay with your mutual fum is still very lucrative, you still have plenty of clients will still be around, but then you're just ignoring a large potential market that's growing up and building their wealth right now. Obviously, in the States, we still do have mutual fund managers who are still doing well. So and as long as we don't have the investment culture here and no one's looking, I think those can sustain in definitely here as well.
turns.zh: 就我个人而言——也许我有偏见——我认为每一家大型资产管理公司都应该拥有 ETF，就是这样。我之所以这么说，是因为你当然可以继续经营共同基金，那项业务仍然利润丰厚，你仍有大量客户，共同基金也会继续存在；但如果只做共同基金，你就忽视了一个正在成长并积累财富的巨大潜在市场。显然，在美国仍有一些共同基金管理人经营得很好。只要欧洲还没有形成投资文化、也没有人关注这一市场，我认为这些机构在这里也能无限期维持下去。

turns.en: So you know, if we kind of stay on the topic of mutual funds, you know, one of the things we've observed here obviously is fees. You know, if we go back thirty years, fees and mutual funds were quite high. I mean they're still kind of high compared to ETFs, but I think the ETF industry has kind of helped kind of lower the average fees in mutual funds. Do you think that could you know, something similar could happen in Europe. You know, if active ETFs really take off, and you know what could that do to the economics. Could the ETF rapper actually force active fees to go lower across the industry?
turns.zh: 既然我们还在谈共同基金，我想说说我们观察到的一个现象，那就是费率。如果回到 30 年前，共同基金的费率相当高；我的意思是，与 ETF 相比，现在仍然有些高。但我认为，ETF 行业帮助降低了共同基金的平均费率。你认为欧洲会发生类似的情况吗？如果主动型 ETF 真正起飞，这会对行业的盈利模式产生什么影响？ETF 载体会不会迫使整个行业的主动管理费率下降？

turns.en: Absolutely? Absolutely, I don't think it's happened yet. The margins is to too lucrative, if I may say, for them to lower any fees.
turns.zh: 绝对会，绝对会。我认为目前还没有发生，因为这些业务的利润率仍然太丰厚了——如果可以这么说的话——所以它们没有动力降低任何费率。

turns.en: But the fact that.
turns.zh: 但事实是——

turns.en: Existing mutual fund as active managers are launching ats at or below JB. Morgan and other active managers tells me that they're cognizant of fees. And once they launched those I think they launched them a little too low there others just to get in because once they launched those, then existing clients or clients who are children of existing clients will start saying, why is there such as discrepancy in your fees? I think that's what will eventually force either the the fees of the mutual funds to come down or maybe, if even possible at this point, a revisit to the ETF fees.
turns.zh: 现有共同基金领域的主动管理人正在以不高于 JPMorgan 和其他主动管理人的费率推出主动型 ETF，这说明它们已经意识到了费率问题。我认为，它们为了进入市场，推出这些产品时把费率定得比其他产品略低了一些。但一旦产品推出，现有客户或现有客户的子女就会开始问：“为什么你们的费率差距这么大？”我认为，最终这会迫使共同基金费率下降，或者——如果到那时还有可能的话——促使行业重新审视 ETF 的费率。

turns.en: But you know, so are the etf acts, I mean, are there fees? Is it similar to the US in terms of fees being much lower on ETFs than mutual funds in Europe.
turns.zh: 不过，欧洲 ETF 的费率呢？我的意思是，欧洲是否和美国类似，ETF 的费率远低于共同基金？

turns.en: To be honest, I haven't really looked too full to have neutral fune fees. What I have seen is that in the US, mainly because of the outcome ETFs. In Europe, active ETFs account for about three point eight percent of assets and they generate about five percent of revenue, so that's pretty close. That tells me that they're launching expense racials close to what the market is, maybe only slightly above, whereas in the States, I think last time I checked it was a twelve percent of assets. We're in active ETFs generating three percent of revenue. So that's a huge discrepancy, right, So are the fees much lower? I think they are much lower than the if you put in like all the registrations and incentive fees absolutely there, they should be much lower. Not to mention, I still I think they still have a lot of entry and as fees too, at least entry fees last time.
turns.zh: 坦率地说，我还没有非常全面地研究共同基金费率。我看到的情况是，在欧洲——主要是由于确定结果型 ETF——主动型 ETF 约占资产规模的 3.8%，贡献约 5% 的收入，这两者相当接近。这说明，它们推出产品时设定的费用率（expense ratio）与市场水平接近，可能只略高一点。相比之下，在美国，我上次查看时，主动型 ETF 约占资产规模的 12%，却贡献了 3% 的收入。这是一个巨大的差距，对吧？那么，ETF 的费率是不是低得多？如果把所有返佣和销售激励费都算进去，我认为它们确实远低于共同基金费率，绝对如此。更不用说，我认为共同基金仍然收取不少申购费和赎回费；至少我上次看的时候，申购费仍然存在。

turns.en: So I kind of you know, actually, the more I think about it, you know, the outcome you know, I think obviously in the US it you know, with passive you know, the fees became so so low, and you know, active is kind of brought up a bit, you know, if we just think about typical security selection active in ETFs, but there's still much lower than mutual funds. But all these outcome and you know, option strategies, some of these managers are kind of you know, they're they're getting away with much higher fees than what we're accustomed to an ETF wrapper. And do you think that could be one reason why a lot of managers are kind of focused on these outcome type products in Europe being able to kind of charge a higher fee.
turns.zh: 我想，越仔细思考就越觉得，确定结果型产品确实很有意思。在美国，被动产品的费率显然已经变得非常低，而主动型产品又把费率略微抬高了一些——这里我们只考虑 ETF 中通常采用证券选择的主动型产品——但它们仍远低于共同基金。不过，所有这些结果导向型策略和期权策略中，有些管理人收取的费率远高于我们过去对 ETF 载体的习惯认知。你认为，这会不会正是许多管理人专注于在欧洲推出这类结果导向型产品的一个原因，也就是能够收取更高费率？

turns.en: Oh yeah, of course, of course I've mentioned it briefly before, but I think it's it's two is one, they can charge more for them, and two, there is a history of structured products here, structure notes, so it's much it'll be uh, it'll be more familiar to the client, but more importantly to the person selling the THETF. They know how to sell these sort of products, right and overall, I think they do address solutions. I think there is a market for them. Issuers see them right now. The I think the biggest challenge to outcome ets in Europe is the infrastructure, right we don't have that many leaps options markets here trading daily bases in in in local hours yet.
turns.zh: 当然，当然。我之前简单提过，我认为原因有两个：第一，它们可以为这类产品收取更高费率；第二，欧洲有结构性产品和结构性票据的历史，因此客户会更熟悉这类产品，更重要的是，销售 ETF 的人也更熟悉。他们知道如何销售这种产品。总体而言，我认为这些产品确实能提供解决方案，也确实存在市场。发行人现在已经看到了这一点。我认为，欧洲确定结果型 ETF 面临的最大挑战是基础设施。这里还没有太多长期期权（LEAPS options）市场，能够在本地交易时段内每日进行交易。

turns.en: So let's let's finish with a prediction. If we fast forward five years, what percentage would you say European ETF assets would be active? And you know, what will we look back on is the development that really caused the market to take off.
turns.zh: 最后，我们用一个预测来结束。如果把时间快进 5 年，你认为欧洲 ETF 资产中会有多大比例属于主动型产品？回头看时，我们会认为是哪项发展真正推动这个市场起飞？

turns.en: You know, I really hate to be at the b downer, but we're still at We went from three point two percent to three point eight percent of assets in the past year. In the next five years, I mean in the States where I don't see us going past five percent, I see the number of etip all the number of ETFs will grow tremendously, but I think there's going to be a lot of fighting for assets and flows for the foresee the future. The only thing that might change though is if we need like one or two maybe three active managers are really knocking on the ballpark, and that'll catch attention, you know, and that might spark a bit more investment culture and then more just in active ETFs. But barring that, I mean, especially and if it's it's I always go back to the cultural part because it also has to be a manager that is from your country. So if it's a German manager who doesn't really I don't know if the French will be too happy about it. And it's a French manager who really axetle evolve hard, I don't know if the Brits were really gravitate towards them. I don't know people gravitate towards towards performance. But there are regional competition here.
turns.zh: 你知道，我真的不想泼冷水，但我们仍处于这样的水平：过去 1 年中，主动型产品占资产规模的比例从 3.2% 上升到 3.8%。未来 5 年，我认为我们不会超过 5%。我预计 ETF 数量会大幅增加，但在可预见的未来，各家产品将为争夺资产和资金流而激烈竞争。唯一可能改变局面的，是出现一两家、或许 3 家主动管理人，真正取得极其出色的表现。那会吸引注意力，也可能进一步激发投资文化，并带来对主动型 ETF 的更多兴趣。但如果没有这种情况——我之所以总是回到文化问题，是因为表现出色的管理人还得来自你所在的国家。如果是一家德国管理人，我不知道法国人会不会特别乐于接受；如果是一家整体表现非常出色的法国管理人，我也不知道英国人是否真的会转向它。或许人们终究会被业绩吸引，但这里确实存在地区间竞争。

turns.en: Okay, so let me just do one more follow up. You know you mentioned in the different markets. So but you know, if we think of a company like JP Morgan, they're across the different European markets, correct, But there are other companies that are really just focused on their individual countries. So do you think that that makes it difficult for like firms to compete? Oh?
turns.zh: 好的，我再追问一个问题。你提到了不同市场。像 JPMorgan 这样的公司覆盖欧洲多个市场，对吧？但还有一些公司实际上只专注于自己的国家。你认为，这会让企业间的竞争变得困难吗？

turns.en: Yeah, of course, so large companies have a definite avantage. But even then JP Morgan, like I mentioned, they have a very well oiled distribution of apparatus if you will. But it's still not easy. You've got different regulators. Even though it's useless, you still have to get approval from all the different regulators, and the translations, the local languages, local listings, times are required. So yeah, if you're big, then you definitely have a leg up. But then that also means that if you're a local manager, you have probably a tighter engagement model with your local clients.
turns.zh: 是的，当然会。所以，大公司拥有明确优势。但即便如此，正如我提到的，JPMorgan 拥有一套运转非常顺畅的渠道分销体系，但这仍然不容易。你要面对不同的监管机构。即便有欧盟可转让证券集合投资计划（Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities, UCITS），你仍然必须获得不同监管机构的批准，还要处理翻译、当地语言版本和当地上市等要求，有时这些都是必要的。所以，如果你的规模很大，肯定会占据优势。但这也意味着，如果你是当地管理人，你与本地客户之间的互动模式可能更加紧密。

turns.en: So it's it's gonna be hard for us managers that aren't that don't have an established footprint in Europe uh to you know, to kind of grow there.
turns.zh: 所以，对于那些尚未在欧洲建立业务基础的美国管理人来说，要在那里实现增长会很困难。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah, of course, but it's not impossible. For example, American Century Avantis, there are they as you know, they're they're active as well, and they're making some good rain roads. But again that's because you know their their distribution team is all over the place, you know, uh, locking up the doors and and opening not just the distribution networks but also structurally and from a really perset. So yes, it's gonna be difficult. It just takes a lot of working. But it's not just work. You have to know it first. So the first stage for an American uh A manager looking to get into Europe is do your research at and figure out, Okay, what is the plan for the distribute and the and how's it different the states? What's your approach? But no, it's it's it will be difficult, but not impossible. Everyone's struggling with the same things.
turns.zh: 是的，当然，但并非不可能。比如 American Century Avantis，你也知道，它们同样采取主动管理，而且正在取得一些不错的进展。但这同样是因为它们的渠道分销团队四处奔走、挨家敲门，不仅打开渠道分销网络，还从架构和监管角度推进工作。所以，是的，这会很困难，需要投入大量工作。但这不只是做多少工作的问题，首先还必须了解市场。因此，对于希望进入欧洲的美国资产管理公司而言，第一步就是做好研究，弄清楚渠道分销计划是什么、欧洲与美国有何不同，以及你准备采取什么方法。不过，虽然困难，却并非不可能；大家都在应对同样的问题。
